Nice music and art style. Gameplay: Age of War 2 the way it should be. However, there are some problems with the game balance. The initial campaign cutscene that blends with gameplay footage looks a bit strange. Overall, pretty good, but it "just needs some squeaking".

[b][u]Update 2025.11.24[/u][/b]: Hello Brian, thanks for your response! I am awfully sorry I could not give a recommendation for the game, because I LOVE rats and really like the artworks and style overall! =,( Regarding your questions: [u][i]Bugs[/i][/u]: I am not sure if they are bugs or issues, but if one "clicks" in "loading screens", like to skip the "cutscene" or to get over the "Ded" sign, the game accepts the input and "shoots" the weapon one has. If one (like myself) has low ammo it really hurts to fire 1-2 rockets of the rocket launcher for no reason. Also when it happens going into the mission, I also damage/ kill my troops which spawn with me in the beginning. The other thing was, that the mouse really easy leaves the monitor where the game is on (I have a big "main monitor" and a really small "auxiliary monitor"). I think I had "borderless fullscreen" on, but many games are able to hold the mouse "in the game", here it often went on the second screen (mayhaps because we have to aim 99% to the right?) and then the game lost focus and I died before I could come back to it. Again, many games I play in borderless mode do not have this issue (Star Citizen, Helldivers 2, Fallout 4 or ARC Raiders), so it was really a problem of WAR RATS (at least for me). Additionally if switching back after loosing focus (either by the mouse leaving the screen or accidentally pressing something like "windows key"), the game "flickers" two to three times, which caused my death one or two times [i][u]Difficulty[/u][/i]: The first three(?) missions were really ok, they got more difficult, but with the right weapons/ good movements/ reinforcements it was clearly beatable. Then the game offered two missions to choose from (going up or down), and even though I chose the map going down with "moderate" difficulty (the top one was "very hard" or similar) I was not able to clear it in over 1 hour. I tried it with different weapon combos, with a lot of aggression, with defensive tactics, with no care regarding my troops, with focus on specific enemies only, etc. Still I was not able to clear it - the mission was clearly 2-4 times harder than any mission before. Additionally the "hitboxes" of my troops and buildings were really in the way in this mission. To shoot over Grunts and Ratineers was no problem overall, but the turrets and "Spirit Rats" are just huge. Even with a lot of jumping around I killed them more often than not (and if I did not try to help them, they were killed even sooner by the enemies). And in case of the turrets I often couldn't even try to help them - only if there was a rock to stand on, but depending on the flow of the battle I was in front of it (so I was in danger of dying) or I was too far behind it and was damaging it myself. The "start of the mission" or gameplay loop was also strange, because if one was about to fail, it was way better to loose it and take as much CHz(?), aka money to buy stuff, with one, because then one could (try to) upgrade abilities and weapons (which were too expensive overall) or at least to get "a headstart" in the next battle. Seems not very intuitive to die deliberately, so the next try is more manageable. Especially if the money is often not enough for upgrades so it is a loop without an escape. [i][u]Progression[/u][/i]: Because of the difficulty (but also the issues), I could not clear maps anymore and so the progression stopped - which was overall a let down. Especially because the money in the mission and in the nest is the SAME one has the strange situation to loose the battle on purpose to get a better second try. At the same time, the amount of mony is not enough to get upgrades, aka to progress, so it feels like a waste of time. Yes, I still got e.g. blueprints, but 1. I struggled to get money for them (and more so for the ammo) and 2. they were not much better than the weapons I already had, so I couldn't break the stalemate I was in. I hope this helps and makes my issues with the game more clear. I will keep an eye on the game and look forward to some updates! Cheers [u]2025.11.23[/u]: One feels the passion and fun, the people had creating this, but small bugs and gameplay issues like difficulty spikes, grind without reward and missing progression, do make it a chore. Wait until it gets some updates/ fixed. I would refund, but I wanted to be sure whether it is the game or me - it was the game. Devs can have the money, next time I will not buy such a game. Edit: Steam accepted my refund although I was over the 2 hours, in this sense: Thanks! Came for the rats, but seems I should leave the sinking ship with them. Shame.

It was somewhat fun for a while but became repetitive quickly and hasn't improved much on the older original games in the genre. I'm not upset that I got it and had some fun but I would not buy it again or recommend it to others. I was persuaded in large part by the very high review score but I'm guessing if the game didn't have a rat theme to meme the score would drop exponentially. I made the purchase after it was out of early access but the game feels like it was definitely released too soon. In a single playthrough sans the final boss: On the soldier recruitment tab there's still a message about more troops coming in early access despite my purchase being after the game left EA, when jumping during combat I once glitched into the sky for a few seconds which almost caused me to die and lose the level. If you have maximum ammo for a gun the game will prevent you from buying more but if you go to buy ammo when you are not at the maximum it will allow you to buy indefinitely wasting your currency if you're not keeping track - the extra ammo will also not remain on the field it will just be lost when you pick it up. The home base you go to between levels is very large and your character moves very slow and there's no way to sprint or dash - they even made a teleporter on the base an upgrade option but that's not a fun thing to upgrade and it still feels slow and tedious to traverse base even with a teleporter. I feel like the base could also be condensed significantly, there are hubs that could be combined and it feels like it was stretched just so there are more things to unlock. There are loot crates that spawn on the field and many of these are near or on top of the areas you are intended to build camps or turrets and when you build them they will often be partially hidden by what you build so you have to carefully try to hit them without damaging the base you just built (some base options are invulnerable to both teams while others can be damaged by both teams). The game will also let you waste currency by building identical items in the same spot such as a cheese collector. It would be nice to see more info on the recruitment tab - such as troop strength, speed, abilities, etc. instead of just cost. Lots of little qol things that just feel like they should have been addressed earlier. In other games I've played similar to this if the hero dies they will respawn after a timer instead of dying causing the loss of the entire level. In those games the real threat for loss of level would be the enemy team breaching your base instead of your hero dying. I'm assuming that can happen here too? but during the entire playthrough for this game though I never once even felt remotely like the enemy could breach the base regardless of my strategy so it was just a matter of not letting my hero die and slowly pushing. I don't mind that the hero dying will instead cause a loss of the level but due to friendly fire in this game your hero needs to be at or near the front and always in harms way to really push. When you fire your weapon behind your own soldiers it will hit them. I thought? I saw a message about turning friendly fire off in the game but didn't see any settings for it. I cleared the final level and reached what I assume was the final boss but I had almost no ammo equipped and there didn't appear to be anyway to actually get more ammo once the encounter started? so I could not possibly have beaten him anyways (unless there's someway to obtain ammo after an extended period of time fighting the boss). This seems like a major oversight. I just didn't feel motivated to go through the entire level again just to challenge the boss. There are new enemies and different aesthetics as the game progresses but it never felt like there was any huge variation in gameplay. This review might seem overly critical and I wouldn't say the game is bad but seeing an overwhelmingly positive score made me think this was going to be a great improvement over previous games and I don't personally think that's the case. I suspect if it wasn't for the theme and generic soldiers were instead used the score would be much lower. If you really like this genre and want something new to play you'll probably feel it is decent but don't I don't think it improved much on games of the past and there were lots of little issues that made it feel like it was not ready for full release.

this game has a lot of heart and soul but i dont think its polished enough to cost money or be called a full release. there are a LOT of bugs, mostly harmless or visual, but occasionally pretty bad (like getting stuck in place or units not targeting enemies killing them). i dont think the units and weapons are very balanced either. i got about 2/3 through the campaign and from what i could tell the best strategy by far was just spamming the cheapest unit (rathound) with items that buff it and spamming a rocket launcher from behind them when there was something with a lot of health. this way i was able to literally just walk through each stage with almost no resistance, but trying to do literally anything else was a brick wall where moving forward was basically impossible. i ignored every building except the campfire (to regen cheese) and the biggest turret to wall off enemies while i made a new batch of rathounds. none of the upgrades or statues feel very impactful because they add very small bonuses for a lot of money, meanwhile dumping cash into units provide an immediate return. the shooting doesnt feel great in general, bullets travel slowly and dont feel punchy when they hit. its just kind of clicking endlessly into bullet sponges. my biggest problem is with the UI, it's very difficult to navigate. weapon and unit stats are mostly hidden, lettering is very small and difficult to read (especially ammo count), and the colors are really drab and dont contrast well so everything just sort of blends together both in the menus and on the battlefield. maybe a clearer distinction between object layers and heavier outlines would solve this? i honestly dont know, just that it was a repeated annoyance and i had trouble keeping track of things on my screen i didnt hate this game by any means and it had some pretty enjoyable features as well (i like the little suicide bomb rat you can throw out) but there were too many annoyances for me to stick around. i could see myself coming back and reevaluating in the future once there has been more polishing and balance passes.

Thoroughly unimpressed with some of the game design choices. I enjoy most things about the game but I think it has some strange design choices. I will finish the game anyway and hopefully I can change my stance. Update for dev response: One of my issues is I personally do not like how its a side scroller game with friendly fire. It makes attacking enemies more difficult and tedious in a way I personally don't find fun. I don't see other people mentioning it which makes me think its a personal problem but I mean I paid for the game I feel fair enough in critiquing it. I appreciate the response and trying to build your game to be better, definitely a breath of fresh air.

Music, art style, and gameplay all feels like an old flash game in the best way possible. There's definitely some bugs, but nothing game breaking and the core gameplay loop is super enjoyable with a fun variety of weapons, equipment, and upgrades. You can beat the game in 5-ish hours, but I got 10 hours of it trying different modes and difficulties and I look forward to revisiting the game for future updates.

If you don't like flash games, or simplistic side-scroller games, you probably won't like this one; but, to those that do, it really is worth asking price. Loved it, 100%ed it, would recommend.
